tagline: The Netherlands' oldest university city has graceful canals, Rembrandt's birthplace, world-class museums and one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world.
overview: Leiden is a canal city between Amsterdam and The Hague, famous for Leiden University, founded in 1575 and the oldest in the Netherlands. Its Rapenburg canal is lined with grand 17th-century houses, and students give the old town a lively feel.

The Hortus Botanicus, founded in 1590, is one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world; it was here that Carolus Clusius planted some of the first tulips in the Netherlands. Leiden also has the National Museum of Antiquities, the Naturalis biodiversity museum and the Museum De Lakenhal.

Rembrandt was born in Leiden in 1606, and the Pilgrims lived here for over a decade before sailing to America. On 3 October the city celebrates the 1574 relief of its Spanish siege with herring, white bread and hutspot stew. More than 100 poems are painted on walls around town.
